science.title: Effect of six weeks of environmental enrichment on oxidative metabolism and hypothalamic mitochondrial markers of adult male mice
science.description: Environmental enrichment (EE) is a non-pharmacological strategy that enhances cognitive, sensory, social, and motor stimulation and has been associated with neuroprotective effects. However, its impact on hypothalamic oxidative metabolism and mitochondrial dynamics in adult animals remains unclear. This study investigated whether six weeks of EE modulates redox balance and mitochondrial markers in the hypothalamus of adult male mice. C57BL/6 mice were maintained in a standard environment (SE) or under EE conditions for six weeks, followed by the assessment of oxidative stress biomarkers, antioxidant defenses, mitochondrial enzymatic activity, and gene expression related to mitochondrial function. EE did not affect body weight but increased food intake. Mitochondrial analysis revealed elevated citrate synthase (CS) activity, with no changes observed in the NAD⁺/NADH ratio. EE reduced protein oxidation, while lipid peroxidation remained unchanged. Antioxidant responses were selectively modulated by increasing catalase (CAT) and glutathione S-transferase (GST) activities, while reduces superoxide dismutase (SOD) activity and the redox state, suggesting adaptive redox remodeling. Gene expression analysis revealed increased PGC-1α levels without changes in TFAM, DRP1, or OPA1, indicating enhanced oxidative capacity without alterations in mitochondrial biogenesis or dynamics. Overall, EE promotes metabolic and redox adaptations in the hypothalamus, improving oxidative efficiency and selectively protecting proteins from oxidative damage.

science.title: Rab4b controls hepatic glucose production during fasting through glycophagy
science.description: Hepatic glucose production, essential for maintaining glycemia, is often altered in metabolic-associated fatty liver and glycogen storage diseases. Therefore, understanding the mechanisms that regulate the glucose production by hepatocyte is pivotal. Recent studies have identified endocytic trafficking as a key modulator of liver glucose production. Particularly, its role in directing protein trafficking toward lysosomal degradation influences gluconeogenesis. However, the contribution of endocytic recycling to liver glucose production remains yet poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that hepatocyte-specific disruption of endocytic recycling, achieved through Rab4b knockout in male, leads to fasting hyperglycemia. Mechanistically, hepatocytes lacking Rab4b exhibit an increased capacity to produce glucose independently of gluconeogenesis by depleting their glycogen stores. This is driven by enhanced glycophagy, leading to excessive glucose release and fasting hyperglycemia. Notably, liver Rab4b expression also correlates with glycemia in both mice and human, highlighting a critical role of Rab4b-dependent endocytic recycling in regulating blood glucose homeostasis during fasting. This study reveals an unexpected role for Rab4b-dependent endocytic recycling in orchestrating the liver’s response to fasting, linking autophagy-driven glycogen breakdown to glucose production.
